rows.answer: Where a lease of immovable property has determined by forfeiture for non-payment of rent, the lessor may sue to eject the lessee, as provided in Section 114 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 [2]. In West Bengal, a landlord may make an application to the Controller for an order or decree for recovery of possession where the tenant has made default in payment of rent for three months within a period of twelve months, or for three rental periods within a period of three years where the rent is not payable monthly, under Section 6 of the West Bengal Premises Tenancy Act, 1997 [10]. In Punjab, a Revenue-officer may cause a notice of ejectment to be served on a tenant for failure to satisfy a decree for an arrear of rent under Section 44 of the Punjab Tenancy Act, 1887 [3]. In the Central Provinces, a decree for an arrear of rent may be executed by the ejectment of the tenant under Section 85 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act, 1898 [7]. In Ajmer, the tahsildar shall cause a notice to be served on the tenant to pay decreed arrears of rent into court under Section 98 of the Ajmer Tenancy and Land Records Act, 1950 [5]. rows.answer: An application for compensation may be made by the person who has sustained the injury, by the owner of the property, by all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased where death has resulted from the accident, or by any agent duly authorised by the person injured or all or any of the legal representatives of the deceased, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2]. Where all the legal representatives of the deceased have not joined in the application, the application shall be made on behalf of or for the benefit of all the legal representatives, and the ones who have not joined shall be impleaded as respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2]. The application shall be made, at the option of the claimant, either to the Claims Tribunal having jurisdiction over the area in which the accident occurred, or to the Claims Tribunal within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the claimant resides or carries on business, or within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the defendant resides, under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 [2]. rows.answer:
Yes, a police officer may arrest you without a warrant if you commit a cognizable offence in their presence, or if there is a reasonable complaint, credible information, or reasonable suspicion that you have committed a cognizable offence [1]. 

Conditions and time limits:
- For offences punishable with imprisonment for a term less than seven years or extending up to seven years, the police officer must have reason to believe you committed the offence and be satisfied that arrest is necessary to prevent further offences, ensure proper investigation, prevent destruction or tampering of evidence, prevent threats or inducements to witnesses, or ensure your presence in court [1].
- For offences punishable with imprisonment of less than three years, no arrest of a person who is infirm or above sixty years of age can be made without the prior permission of an officer not below the rank of Deputy Superintendent of Police [1].
- If an arrest is not required under Section 35(1) of The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the police officer must issue a notice directing you to appear before them or at a specified place [1].

rows.question: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?
queries: I lent my friend money three years ago. Is it too late to file a case to get it back?
suit for recovery of money limitation period debt
Limitation Act section 19 effect of payment on limitation
Limitation Act article 21 money lent payable at fixed time demand
rows.answer:
For money payable for money lent, the period of limitation is three years, and the time from which the period begins to run is when the loan is made, as provided under Article 19 of The Limitation Act, 1963 [3].

For money lent under an agreement that it shall be payable on demand, the period of limitation is three years, and the time from which the period begins to run is when the loan is made, as provided under Article 21 of The Limitation Act, 1963 [4].

When the lender has given a cheque for the money, the period of limitation is three years, and the time from which the period begins to run is when the cheque is paid, as provided under Article 20 of The Limitation Act, 1963 [5].

Where payment on account of a debt is made before the expiration of the prescribed period by the person liable or by his duly authorized agent, a fresh period of limitation shall be computed from the time when the payment was made, provided that an acknowledgment of the payment appears in the handwriting of, or in a writing signed by, the person making the payment, as provided under Section 19 of The Limitation Act, 1963 [1].

rows.answer:
You are protected by Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, which makes it an offence punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years and also a liability to fine when a husband or his relative subjects a woman to cruelty [1]. You are also protected by the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005, under which a Magistrate can pass protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, custody orders, or compensation orders, and grant interim and ex parte orders [4][6].

Conditions and time limits:
- The Magistrate shall fix the first date of hearing not ordinarily beyond three days from the date of receipt of the application [4].
- The Magistrate shall endeavour to dispose of every application within a period of sixty days from the date of its first hearing [4].

Related provisions:
- Section 220 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, regarding the prosecution and cognizance of offences under Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [7].

rows.question: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?
queries: Can I file for divorce in the first year of marriage?
divorce before completion of one year of marriage exceptional hardship

rows.answer:
It shall not be competent for any court to entertain any petition for dissolution of a marriage by a decree of divorce unless at the date of the presentation of the petition one year has elapsed since the date of the marriage, as provided under Section 14 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 [1]. Similarly, no petition for divorce shall be presented to the district court unless at the date of the presentation of the petition one year has passed since the date of entering the certificate of marriage in the Marriage Certificate Book under Section 29 of the Special Marriage Act, 1954 [2], and no suit for divorce by mutual consent shall be filed unless at the date of the filing of the suit one year has lapsed since the date of the marriage under Section 32B of the Parsi Marriage and Divorce Act, 1936 [7].

rows.question: cheque bounce ho gaya kya karu
queries: cheque bounce ho gaya kya karu
dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds notice liability
Negotiable Instruments Act section 138 dishonour of cheque
Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita section 223 prosecution of offences under section 138 Negotiable Instruments Act
topSources: The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 s223
rows.answer:
A person commits an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 when a cheque drawn on their bank account for the discharge of a legally enforceable debt or other liability is returned unpaid by the bank due to insufficient funds or because it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid by agreement [1]. Such an offence is punishable with imprisonment for up to two years, a fine up to twice the amount of the cheque, or both [1].

Conditions and time limits:
- The cheque must be presented to the bank within six months from the date it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier [1].
- The payee or holder in due course must make a demand for payment by giving a written notice to the drawer within thirty days of receiving information from the bank that the cheque was returned unpaid [1].
- The drawer of the cheque must fail to make the payment within fifteen days of receiving the said notice [1].

Related provisions:
- Section 140 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 specifies that it shall not be a defence in a prosecution under section 138 that the drawer had no reason to believe the cheque may be dishonoured [9].

rows.answer:
Whoever fraudulently or dishonestly makes use of the electronic signature, password, or any other unique identification feature of any other person shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to rupees one lakh under Section 66C of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [1][8]. Whoever cheats by personating by means of any communication device or computer resource shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years and shall also be liable to fine which may extend to one lakh rupees under Section 66D of the Information Technology Act, 2000 [2]. Any offence of cheating where the deception is practised by means of electronic communications or letters or telecommunication messages may be inquired into or tried by any Court within whose local jurisdiction such electronic communications or letters or messages were sent or were received under Section 202 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 [3].

Regarding cheating, Section 318 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 provides that whoever by deceiving any person fraudulently or dishonestly induces them to deliver any property commits cheating, and the schedule of the Fugitive Economic Offenders Act, 2018 lists Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 alongside offences under the Indian Penal Code, 1860 such as Section 420 for cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property [9].

rows.question: Is a contract signed by a 16 year old valid, and can a child be punished for a crime?
queries: Is a contract signed by a 16 year old valid, and can a child be punished for a crime?
competency to contract age of majority minor agreement void
Indian Contract Act section 11 capacity of parties
juvenile conflict with law child in conflict with law age responsibility Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita
topSources: Binding Apprentices Act, 1850, 19 of 1850 (Rep., Act 52 of 1961) s25
The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015. s21
The Children Act, 1960, 60 of 1960, (Rep., Act 53 of 1986) s21
rows.answer:
A contract signed by a 16-year-old is not valid because a person must be of the age of majority according to the law to which they are subject to be competent to contract, as stated in Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 [1]. Regarding punishment for a crime, a child above seven years and under twelve years of age with immature understanding does not commit an offence, as provided in Section 21 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 [2].

Conditions and time limits:
- For contractual competence, a person must be of the age of majority, of sound mind, and not disqualified by any law [1][7].
- For criminal responsibility regarding a child between seven and twelve years, the child must not have attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of their conduct on that occasion [2].

- The complaint may be filed by the consumer to whom the goods are sold or delivered, under Section 12 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 [4].

- The complaint shall be instituted in a District Forum within the local limits of whose jurisdiction the opposite party actually and voluntarily resides, carries on business, has a branch office, personally works for gain, or where the cause of action wholly or in part arises, under Section 11 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 [4].

rows.question: notice period for cheque bounce
queries: notice period for cheque bounce
dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds notice demanding payment
Negotiable Instruments Act section 138 notice period
Negotiable Instruments Act section 138 proviso b notice within thirty days
rows.answer:
The notice demanding payment for a bounced cheque must be given in writing within thirty days of the receipt of information by the payee or holder in due course from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 [1]. As explained in the Supreme Court judgment in *Kamlesh Kumar versus State of Bihar & Anr.*, after the cheque is returned unpaid, notice has to be issued within 30 days of the receipt of information in this behalf [11].

Conditions and time limits:
- The cheque must have been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier, under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 [1].
- The written notice demanding payment must be given to the drawer within thirty days of receiving information from the bank that the cheque was returned unpaid, under Section 138 ofmyItem the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 [1].
- The drawer of the cheque has fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice to make the payment, under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 [1].
